methodological_rigor.justification: Single-center descriptive case series of only 9 patients with pathologically confirmed Biliary NEC over 13 years, supplemented by a narrative literature review of 15 articles (17 patients). The authors appropriately note that multivariable analysis was not possible due to sample size. Kaplan-Meier OS is reported with a 95% CI (85-1213 days) that is extremely wide given n=9. Patient flow (Figure 1) is documented. No formal systematic review protocol or PRISMA-style reporting for the literature review component; exclusions are subjective and not counted. The literature review date range is partially redacted.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Biliary NEC is rare and under-reported; even small case series contribute to collective experience and may inform MDT discussions. The paper reinforces that platinum-based chemotherapy is associated with longer survival in reported cohorts (18 vs 9 months). As a single-center case series of 9 patients plus narrative review, LoE maps to 4.

reporting_quality.justification: Neither STROBE nor PRISMA is referenced. Case series reporting (appropriate standards would include CARE for case reports or case-series-specific guidance) is not cited. Detailed per-patient tables and swimmer plots are appropriate. Ethics approval was waived per institutional regulations for retrospective anonymized data, which is explicitly stated. No data availability statement; individual-level data are presumably in tables. Immunohistochemistry description is adequate.

novelty_literature.justification: Biliary NEC case series have been published extensively (refs 13-26 cited are case reports/series; Chu 2020, Zhou 2021, Lee 2020 provide larger institutional cohorts; Ayabe 2019 and Karim 2023 SEER analyses). The incremental contribution is nine additional cases from one Chinese center with integrated literature comparison, which is confirmatory rather than novel.

writing_presentation.justification: Writing is clear and well-organized, with standard IMRaD structure, informative tables and figures (including swimmer plot, KM curve, representative IHC panel). The abstract appropriately caveats the descriptive nature and limited sample. Grammar and terminology are consistent. Minor redacted text in abstract and literature review date range is a cosmetic issue.

key_strengths: Adds nine pathologically confirmed Biliary NEC cases with detailed clinicopathologic, immunohistochemical (Syn, CgA, CD56, Ki-67), and surgical data to a rare-disease literature
Appropriately hedged interpretation: authors explicitly state findings are descriptive and not statistically conclusive
Integrated comparison with published case reports (17 patients across 15 articles) providing qualitative context on platinum-based chemotherapy survival advantage (approximately 18-20 vs 9-10 months)
Transparent patient selection flow diagram (62 screened -> 9 included)
Swimmer plot and KM curve convey individual course and aggregate survival clearly
key_concerns: n=9 precludes meaningful statistical inference; median OS 95% CI of 85-1213 days is uninformative
Literature review is narrative, not systematic (no PRISMA, partial date-range redaction, no risk-of-bias assessment of included case reports)
No molecular profiling (genomic or immune microenvironmental), limiting translational impact
Waived ethics approval may be appropriate institutionally but would benefit from explicit statement of the waiver document/number
Chemotherapy administered only at recurrence (4 of 9), not adjuvantly, limiting assessment of perioperative strategy
Incremental novelty over existing SEER and multicenter analyses (Chu 2020, Zhou 2021, Karim 2023)
chief_reviewer.rationale: Well-written but very small single-center case series with confirmatory findings in a rare malignancy; suitable for a lower-tier oncology or case-series-oriented journal after minor revisions.
